data.title: Bank of Japan Raises Interest Rate to 31-Year High
data.description:
The Bank of Japan has raised its trendsetting interest rate by 25 basis points to 1.25%, the highest level since 1995. The central bank's governors voted 7-2 in favor of the interest rate increase, which was widely expected by economists and analysts. Financial markets had priced in a 90% chance that the Bank of Japan would raise interest rates by 25 basis points.

In a statement, the central bank said higher rates are needed because there's a risk that inflation will move above its 2% annualized target. The latest rate hike comes amid rising inflation in Japan as well as a historically weak yen currency. Japan's inflation rate rose to an annualized rate of 1.9% in August. The yen currency dipped 0.45%, while the benchmark 10-year Japanese government bond yield fell 4.9 basis points to 2.947% after the interest rate increase was announced.

U.S. Concerns Related to Japan

Japan's interest rate hike comes days after the U.S. Federal Reserve also lifted its key rate by 25-basis points to counter inflation. It was the first rate increase in America in three years. Inflation in the U.S. has been above the central bank's 2% annualized target for more than five years. Fed Chair Kevin Warsh has struck a hawkish tone on inflation.

data.title: U.S. Government Approves Sale of Lockheed Martin (LMT) F-35 Fighter Jet to Saudi Arabia
data.description:
The administration of U.S. President Donald Trump has approved the sale to Saudi Arabia of 50 F-35 fighter jets made by defense contractor Lockheed Martin (LMT). The deal is worth $24.3 billion and comes as Middle East tensions rise and the kingdom faces intensifying attacks from the Iran-backed Houthis in Yemen.

Lockheed Martin's F-35 jet is widely viewed as the world's most advanced fighter aircraft and is capable of stealth activities and flying undetected by radar. "This proposed sale will support a major non-NATO ally that is a force for political stability and economic progress in the Gulf region," said the U.S. State Department in a statement.

data.title: Nvidia Stock (NVDA) Slips as Huawei Accelerates an AI Chip Launch
data.description:
Nvidia (NVDA) stock slipped slightly on Friday alongside news that semiconductor rival Huawei has accelerated the release of a new chip. It appears that Huawei wants to challenge Nvidia directly with the release of its Ascend 960DT chip. This chip was originally set to be released in Q4 2027, but has now had its release date moved up to Q1 2027.

Huawei is directly challenging Nvidia with the release of this new chip. Nvidia has been the dominant player in the AI chip space, but hasn't been able to obtain a strong foothold in China. That's largely due to export bans on powerful chips that were put in place by the U.S. government. As a result, chipmakers in China, such as Huawei, are accelerating their chip developments to fill the gap left by export restrictions.

What This Means for Nvidia

Even with export bans and increased competition, Nvidia isn't likely going to struggle to grow its AI business. CEO Jensen Huang recently noted that the company expects its year-over-year chip sales to double in 2027. This comes as President Donald Trump continues to push AI development as a focal point for the U.S., despite warnings from AI company CEOs that development needs to slow.

If those rumors are true, it would leave semiconductor rival Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) with the only next-generation GPU release in 2027.

data.title: Tesla Stock (TSLA) Slips Despite Launching Hunt for Chinese Optimus Suppliers
data.description:
Shares in EV maker Tesla (TSLA) were lower today despite reports that it is auditing potential Chinese suppliers to get ready to ramp up in the production of its Optimus humanoid robot at the end of this year. According to an article in the South China Morning Post Tesla officials and engineers have already started auditing companies such as heat-control component manufacturer Zhejiang Sanhua Intelligent Controls, auto parts supplier Ningbo Joyson Electronic, and chassis producer Tuopu Group. As part of the audit it will be looking at a company's production and compliance standards.

Substantial Supply Chain Challenge

It is understood that most of the firms being examined by Tesla already provide components used in its electric car fleet. The Post said that Tesla is planning to place additional orders for components following the start of Optimus production at its the Fremont, California factory, using space previously occupied by Model S and Model X lines.

Musk has described humanoid production as substantial, giving the need for innovative components and the lack of an existing supply chain. Indeed, he has called the Optimus humanoid robot Tesla's "biggest product ever."

One option is to make robots in China. Tesla's Chinese boss Allan Wang Hao said earlier this year that its Shanghai Gigafactory had the potential to produce humanoid robots benefiting from China's complete supply chain and advanced manufacturing techniques.

"The audits show that those Chinese suppliers are an important part of Optimus' supply chain," said Chen Jinzhu, CEO of the Shanghai Mingliang Auto Service consultancy. "They enjoy cost and technological advantages over their domestic and overseas rivals."

China is the Driving Force

Indeed, China has to date been the driving force behind the growth of humanoid robots. RBC Capital Markets forecasts a global total addressable market for humanoids of $9 trillion by 2050, with China accounting for more than 60%. That is for use in the home, at work, healthcare and in defense.

Musk, however, is adamant that Optimus can compete. He has said that the first Optimus robots will be used inside Tesla to gather training data and improve the robot before a wider rollout.

data.title: Cheniere Energy Shares Drop 2.8% Over 5 Days Following Suspected LNG Tanker Cyberattack
data.description:
Cheniere Energy (LNG) stock dropped 2.8% over the past five days to $270.97 as news emerged that a tanker bringing U.S. oil (CM:CL) and gas to Europe suffered a suspected cyberattack. The Vivit Africa LNG vessel picked up its gas cargo from Louisiana's Cameron LNG terminal and sailed across the Atlantic toward Italy. However, the crew lost access to internal monitoring systems while traveling through the Mediterranean Sea.

The crew reported the incident to the Korean Register, which serves as safety adviser to the South Korean-owned vessel. Trading firm Vitol Group holds the ship under a long-term lease but declined to share further details. Following the system failure, the ship idled off the Italian coast before turning away from its destination port in Rovigo to head toward Algeciras, Spain.

Maritime Authorities Are Monitoring Security Risks

The Italian Coast Guard stepped in to help after the captain reported a breakdown in cargo tracking screens. Local officials warned nearby ships to keep their distance so everyone stayed safe on the water. The ship uses control gear from Kongsberg Maritime, but company reps said it is still too early to tell what caused the system failure.

This issue follows similar security scares from late August, when U.S. officers boarded two tankers off the American coast over cyber concerns. Federal teams are now watching nearly 20 ships around the world for similar threats. Neither ship owner H-Line Shipping nor the Korean Register answered calls for comment as teams look into the event.

LNG Stock Drops on the News

Traders pushed Cheniere Energy shares down 2.8% over five days as fears grew about cyber risks across global shipping routes. While a single ship delay rarely hurts a huge gas producer, events like this point to bigger industry headaches. When hackers mess with ship systems, insurance costs rise and deliveries get delayed. Oil and gas prices also experience volatility on public markets.

If LNG's shipping lines have to spend more money fixing tech issues and checking vessels, profits take a direct hit. On top of that, choppy oil and gas prices, as well as political tensions in Europe & the Middle east, make investors nervous about owning energy stocks right now. Until safety teams clear up what happened to the Vivit Africa LNG, traders are choosing to play it safe and pull money out of the stock.

data.title: JPMorgan Chase (JPM) Abandons Oil Price Forecast as 'Redlines Crossed'
data.description:
JPMorgan Chase (JPM) has given up on its crude oil price forecast as the Iran war drags on into its seventh month. In a note to clients, Natasha Kaneva, head of global commodities strategy at JPMorgan, wrote: "For the first time since the start of the Iran conflict, we don't have a baseline view… We simply don't know how to model the endgame."

JPMorgan assumed at the start of the war that several "economic redlines" would force U.S. President Donald Trump into an agreement to reopen the Strait of Hormuz waterway, where 20% of the world's oil is typically transported. Those redlines that JPMorgan had forecast included crude oil prices above $100, retail gas prices near $5 a gallon, and the 10-year Treasury yield above 5%.

"Six months later, many of those lines have been crossed, yet the exit strategy is less clear, not more," said JPMorgan's Kaneva.

The U.S. and Iran had reached an interim deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz in June, but that agreement quickly collapsed and fighting has resumed.

Crude oil prices are now above $100 U.S., gas prices are above $5 U.S. a gallon in many U.S. cities, and the 10-year Treasury yield rose above 5% earlier this week.

At the same time, the price of diesel fuel is above $6 U.S. per gallon, a record high.

JPMorgan notes that there are no signs from the U.S. or Iran that they're ready to de-escalate the fighting and get the Strait of Hormuz reopened,

Exacerbating the situation, Ukraine continues to strike Russian oil refineries, driving global energy prices higher.

JPMorgan estimates that the fair price for Brent crude oil, the international standard, is about $90 U.S. per barrel. But it is currently trading near $105 U.S. a barrel.

But where prices go from here, and how the Iran war ends, is anyone's guess, according to the bank.

JPM stock has gained 12% over the last year to trade at $349.31 U.S. per share.

data.title: Tobacco Giant Phillip Morris (PM) Raises Dividend 9% as It Ramps Up Shareholder Rewards
data.description:
Phillip Morris (PM) has raised its quarterly dividend by 9% as it continues to focus on shareholder rewards. Going forward, the tobacco giant will pay a quarterly distribution to stockholders of $1.60 per share, up 8.8% from the previous dividend of $1.47. The new payout gives PM stock a forward yield 3.36% based on the current share price.

Phillip Morris' next dividend is payable on Oct. 26 to shareholders of record as of Oct. 2. The latest hike continues the company's streak of increasing its dividend every year since becoming a public company in 2008. Over the past 18 years, Phillip Morris has raised its dividend a total of 248%, or by a compound annual growth rate of 7.2%.

Rewarding PM Stockholders

Phillip Morris continues to prioritize shareholder rewards. Over the last decade, Philip Morris has returned $75 billion back to its shareholders through dividends and also stock buybacks. The company has spent nearly $1 billion ($984 million) on share repurchases, in addition to ratcheting up its dividend payouts.
